title: Zuckerberg's AI-for-all pitch faces a big problem
excerpt: Meta's Mark Zuckerberg spent 6,500 words explaining why he wants everyone to embrace AI, and how he's willing to throw money at people to get them on board.
content_html:
The guy who got everyone using social media now wants everyone on board with AI.

Mark Zuckerberg made the case for AI-for-all in an impassioned, 6,500-word blog. (Exhibit A: People who need editors.)

Zuckerberg's post laid out his vision for an AI future and why he doesn't think we should all be afraid of it.

He joins a growing cohort of tech executives, including Anthropic's Dario Amodei and Microsoft's Satya Nadella, who are writing lengthy essays on AI's impact on the future.

Zuckerberg's post wasn't random. It coincided with Meta's launch of a new agentic AI model, Muse Glimmer. The model is open-weight, meaning users can download and modify it for free on their own computers. More details on all things Glimmer.

His AI opus highlights the growing debate in the tech community over whether AI models should be open or closed.

Supporters of open-weight models say allowing developers to tinker benefits the entire industry. Those in favor of closed models say the tech is too powerful to make it widely accessible.

Both arguments have their flaws. If your company doesn't have one of the top models, it's easy to support opening up models for everyone. You're not giving up much of a competitive edge.

Meanwhile, top AI companies are struggling to contain their top models. That raises the question: Can you argue you should be the only ones in charge of your models when you're not doing a good job of controlling them in the first place?

Zuckerberg's AI-for-all pitch faces a big problem.

People have strong feelings about AI and the infrastructure that supports it, such as data centers. One way he's trying to get around that is by giving out lots of money.

Meta is creating a $1 billion fund for communities where it is building AI data centers. (Hat tip to my colleague Peter Kafka, who suggested Meta do something like this a few weeks ago.)

A 6,500-word blog post. Multiple media stops. A $1 billion fund. That's a lot of time and effort to get people using AI agents.

But what other choice does Meta have?

The company is built on everyday people using its products (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp) and then selling companies access to their attention. It's not as if Meta can completely upend its business model and start selling AI automation tools to companies.

In some ways, that's fine. AI agents can be a good fit for Meta's user base. The company has a ton of data on individuals that AI can use to become their highly personalized assistants.

But you've got to get people comfortable with using AI in the first place.

Dan DeFrancesco

content_html_zh:
那个让每个人都使用社交媒体的人现在希望每个人都使用人工智能。

马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 在一篇充满激情的 6,500 字博客中阐述了人工智能为所有人服务的理由。 （图表 A：需要编辑的人。）

扎克伯格的帖子阐述了他对人工智能未来的愿景，以及为什么他认为我们不应该害怕它。

他加入了越来越多的科技高管队伍，其中包括 Anthropic 的 Dario Amodei 和微软的 Satya Nadella，他们正在撰写有关人工智能对未来影响的长文。

扎克伯格的帖子并不是随意的。 与此同时，Meta 推出了新的代理人工智能模型 Muse Glimmer。 该模型是开放式的，这意味着用户可以在自己的计算机上免费下载和修改它。 有关 Glimmer 的更多详细信息。

他的人工智能作品凸显了科技界关于人工智能模型应该开放还是封闭的日益激烈的争论。

开放权重模型的支持者表示，允许开发人员进行修补有利于整个行业。 那些支持封闭模式的人表示，这项技术过于强大，无法广泛普及。

这两种论点都有其缺陷。 如果您的公司没有顶级模型之一，那么很容易支持向所有人开放模型。 您并没有放弃太多竞争优势。

与此同时，顶级人工智能公司正在努力遏制他们的顶级模型。 这就提出了一个问题：当你一开始就没有很好地控制模型时，你能说你应该是唯一负责模型的人吗？

扎克伯格的“全民人工智能”计划面临着一个大问题。

人们对人工智能和支持它的基础设施（例如数据中心）有着强烈的感情。 他试图解决这个问题的一种方法是捐赠大量资金。

Meta 正在为正在建设人工智能数据中心的社区创建一个 10 亿美元的基金。 （向我的同事彼得·卡夫卡致敬，他几周前建议 Meta 做这样的事情。）

一篇 6,500 字的博客文章。 多家媒体停播。 10亿美元的基金。 让人们使用人工智能代理需要花费大量的时间和精力。

但Meta还有什么其他选择呢？

该公司的基础是人们每天都使用其产品（Facebook、Instagram、WhatsApp），然后向公司出售吸引他们注意力的机会。 Meta 似乎无法完全颠覆其商业模式并开始向公司销售人工智能自动化工具。

从某些方面来说，这很好。 人工智能代理非常适合 Meta 的用户群。 该公司拥有大量个人数据，人工智能可以利用这些数据成为他们高度个性化的助手。

但首先你必须让人们习惯使用人工智能。
